this time I skip the denial play. Sealing a bore only gives me 1 shelf point and buries a 2-point floor for someone — a net +1 for me but locks the floor from ever being contested. Instead I leave bores 1, 2, 4, 5 open and accept that seat 2 will likely bury my floor next turn. The floors are already mine; the real question is whether I can get a second floor elsewhere. On turn 7 I still have 2 small and 3 large, so I have the inventory to do something — but the only legal moves are large. Picking bore 3 (my own floor) is the worst, since it just buries my own 2-pointer for 1 shelf. Of the remaining, bore 2 is the next seat 0 floor in the sequence and mirrors what seat 2 did to me last game — at least this time I am the one burying their floor on my turn rather than watching it happen. The structural problem is the same: I have no small available to claim a second floor this turn, so the large placements are pure denial. Between equal denial plays I pick the one that takes out seat 0 (currently leading with 4) on bore 2, the next active floor in rotation
